hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Boot with --configPath <tmp>/elsewhere/config.yaml containing requestOverrides (or promptPlaceholder/claude.enableSystemPromptCache), drive one chat-completion request at the recording peer, and assert the provider received the override header. It fails today; a second case uses --dataRoot <tmp>/mounted/data with config.yaml in the install root. It is only a defect for a supported, documented launch flag; if the product decided --configPath is not supported for the chat route it would have to be refused rather than silently defaulted, and it is neither.

hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Two controlled-peer cases: (1) chain https origin -> different host -> a subdomain of the origin, and assert the peer at hop 2 never sees Authorization (pinned deletes, Go re-copies); (2) a 302 on a POST and assert the GET at the target carries Content-Type: application/json as node-fetch does. Both are single-process httptest cases in the existing redirect test file.
hypotheses.counterargument: The credential can only be re-sent to a domain that is still a domain/subdomain of the original provider, so the practical leak surface is the provider's own infrastructure, not a third party. The body-header half is cosmetic unless a provider/WAF distinguishes GET+Content-Type; both are parity defects rather than confirmed third-party leaks, which is why this is sixth rather than in the top five.
